bug.title: The signal author crashes on an authoring config with temperature null: it calls float(self._config.temperature)
bug.symptoms: `./run.sh campaign --type Type-R --workspaces 4 --rounds 2 --width 2` with authoring pins on claude-opus-5-5 / claude-sonnet-5-5, "temperature": null and "effort": "high" (the config providers.load_authoring_config accepts) exits 1 with the one stderr line "float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'". No campaign event is printed. signal_agent/_llm_author.py builds providers.Request with temperature=float(self._config.temperature) at three sites (lines ~379, ~455, ~625).
bug.reproduction_steps: Build the composed "signal-author" with an AuthoringConfig whose temperature is None and ask it to author a root: TypeError from float(None).
bug.expected: - When the config's temperature is None, the signal author builds its Request without stating a temperature. The provider backend decides per model (providers._anthropic already omits sampling for models that reject it). It never calls float(None). - When the config states a temperature, it is passed unchanged, as today. - The authored record's agent_sampling (what orchestrator._roots persists via attempt_provenance_terms) records exactly what was sent: no "temperature" key when none was sent, and the effort when one was sent. It never records a value the vendor did not receive. - test_llm_author_sampling.py drives the root, child and retry authoring paths (all three call sites) with a recording provider: - temperature None gives no crash, and the request carries no explicit temperature - a stated temperature is passed through - agent_sampling matches the sent request in both cases No network, no credential, and it passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: _llm_author.py coerces the config's temperature with float() unconditionally. Feature 5 made that field Optional without updating this caller.
bug.constraints: No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: The configured authoring effort never reaches the Anthropic API: the live registry builds AnthropicProvider without it
bug.symptoms: providers._live builds AnthropicProvider(api_key, model=model, transport=transport) (line ~296) with no effort, although AnthropicProvider accepts effort= and providers._anthropic._request_body sends output_config.effort only when it is given. An authoring config with "effort": "high" therefore authors at the model's default effort (medium on claude-opus-5-5), while the node's agent_sampling may say otherwise.
bug.reproduction_steps: Compose the authoring session from an AuthoringConfig with effort "high" and a recording transport, author once on claude-opus-5-5, and inspect the request body: no output_config.effort.
bug.expected: - The authoring config's effort is threaded from the AuthoringConfig, through the authoring session, to the live registry and into AnthropicProvider for every role (root_tier, depth and policy pins). The request body then carries output_config: {effort: <level>} exactly when the config names one and the model accepts effort. - With no effort configured, nothing is sent (unchanged). - The served-model check and the per-pin budget wrapper are unchanged. - agent_sampling for the authored node names the effort that was actually in the request body. - test_live_registry_effort.py uses a recording transport and an AuthoringConfig with effort "high". It asserts the request body carries output_config.effort == "high" and no temperature for claude-opus-5-5, that a config without effort sends no output_config, and that the authored record's agent_sampling carries "effort": "high". No network, no credential.
bug.actual: Root cause: feature 5 added effort to AuthoringConfig and AnthropicProvider but not to the registry/session path that constructs providers for live authoring.
bug.constraints: No file outside the three listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
